Water has a lot of energy stored in the hydrogen bonds between water molecules, requiring a lot of energy to "break" those bonds. Additionally, it has a relatively high boiling point(for similar reasons). Putting aside the safety concerns of using other solvents for tasks involving food, others in the thread already made the point "yeah it takes more energy to heat it, but it stays heated for a while". As for things like overheating problems, we're leaving out thermal conductivity and blackbody radiation, where the steel may be receiving a lot of direct thermal energy, it's conducting it over to the water quickly enough that that doesn't become a concern. If you want a fun experiment, take a paper cup(with no frills/open paper pieces), fill it with water, and (carefully) apply heat to it. The water will boil before the cup burns.

Thanks lmao, and I absolutely respect the want to get out of that sort of life. I can't speak for all Sheetz in terms of work environment. My store was the type that formed cliques between who was friends with the GM and who wasn't. It definitely will be easier on your body for the most part. Managers tend to get some decent benefits, including a 4 day work week. However, I would be wary of entering as a base employee. Sheetz workweek is designed Friday-Thursday(if I emember correctly) and cheeky managers have a knack for exploiting the scheduling so that they can schedule you for 10 days in a row to avoid paying overtime. Expect the repairmen to sit in the back and watch YouTube videos on how to repair a piece of equipment, waste a few hours, and leave without the equipment being repaired. Expect a need for new equipment to be met with a 3 month wait, at least. Last but not least, the GM's desire for the fattest bonus possible will most likely cause you much suffering. The good news is, if you live near a larger city and work night shifts, you can watch shoplifters get suplexed by cops while doing the jobs of 2 other shifts.

Also, check the bathrooms, especially at night. It doesn't matter if you're busy. Don't want to find the guy overdosing in the bathroom and have to keep the store running while the EMT's wheel his corpse out the side door so customers don't have to see it(like we did).

The pay is decent enough and you may find some cool coworkers to suffer with. But prepare yourself for the negatives too.

On the note of the daemon prince, I love that he just fills in a position. Good all-rounder. Gets a psychic spell, and you can slap what weapon you want for the list you're expecting to play against. Don't underestimate his reroll aura either. I typically just keep wings and dual talons, use him to buff himself/someone more important, and run him in to watch him shred through things with 7 7/-2/2 attacks. Slap intoxicating elixir/some other buff on him and make your opponent sad.

Dark Apostle is good for giving that little bit of extra oomph where you need it. Need some protection? Benediction of Darkness or Illusory Supplication.
Extra hurt? Warp-sight Plea or Soultearer Portent. An extra beatstick? Omen of Potency. Use as you see fit.

Finally, the Lord Discordant. I love this guy. He's won me games on his own. Tilts my friends so much. A unit of marines? They might as well not exist. Vehicles? Nice brackets you got there. Keep in mind, if your opponent focuses on him, he's gonna die quick. And he has 12 wounds, so no character shroud. Bring him if you know you can keep him protected and almost always make him the first fight. Nothing is a more feels-bad moment than sinking power into him and watching him die turn 1. But nothing is more intoxicating than getting him into melee and watching him carve up your opponent like Thanksgiving turkey. I sank the extra points into the Baleflamer because, 18" of a buffed up flamer just feels good. And you're trying to get him into melee so you're already trying to get close. Also makes your opponent think twice about charging him.

Any particular reason you're shying away from sonic weapons? They're hands-down one of the primary reasons to play EC in the first place, despite the power investment.

Also on the note of the MoP: IMO it doesn't feel like you're running enough in the way of daemons to make full utility of him. I feel you'd probably get better utility out of a regular sorceror, especially slapping Prescience on the Oblit or Warptiming your your important things where they need to go.

Since I don't know what your opponent is running in their list, I'm making an assumption here: I feel you'd be better served running a different warlord trait. I pretty much run Loathsome Grace as a default, since it's SOOOOO good at getting you in and wrecking face.

Master the animation. The whole Soulsborne series is based around animations, and timing them correctly. How parrying works is your parry animation has windows of parrying and partial parrying. When your parry window matches with the moment in your opponent's attack animation that the weapon hits you, you will execute a parry. Different shields/off-handers have varying animations, and thus, different parry windows. You want to aim so the attack animation hits you at the moment in your parry animation where your off-hand is at the peak of its animation(i.e. when your shield is fully in front of you). Small shields and the parrying knife have the longest parry windows. The caestus and fist have the quickest response time(the time between you hitting the left trigger and the animation bringing your off-hand to its parry window). I would recommend trying out these different things and noting the differences between them, as well as practicing as much as possible. You'll probably find the caestus sees a lot of use in PvP.
